cards.text: Jesus and the people traveling with Him are on the road again, and He comes into a village. Somebody there is about to open their door to Him. Friend, imagine Jesus showing up at YOUR door when your living room looks like the junk drawer I used to live in.

cards.question: In this village, a woman named Martha welcomes Jesus into her ___.

cards.text: Martha has a sister named Mary. And while the whole house is buzzing, Mary heads straight for the guest of honor.

cards.question: Martha's sister Mary finds a spot near Jesus. What does she do there?

answers.text: Sits at His feet listening to Him
Brings Him a bowl of fresh water
Asks Him to bless the whole house

cards.text: But Martha is distracted by all the preparations to be made. I KNOW that look, friend. That's me with four timers going off at once and my apron on backwards.

cards.question: Martha comes to Jesus and asks if He doesn't care about something. What is it?

answers.text: That her sister left her to serve alone
That the house is too small for everyone
That His followers came without warning

cards.question: True or false: Martha asks Jesus to tell Mary to help her.

cards.text: "Martha, Martha," the Lord replies. When somebody says your name TWICE, you put down whatever you're holding. Spoon, dish towel, everything. Down.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus tells Martha she is worried and upset about many things.

cards.text: Many things. Martha's got a list as long as my apron strings. Then Jesus tells her how much is really needed.

cards.question: Jesus tells Martha that only ___ thing is necessary.
Then Jesus talks about what Mary has chosen. What does He say about it?

answers.text: It will not be taken away from her
She has to set it aside for now
She can have it once the work is done

cards.question: True or false: Jesus sends Mary off to help Martha with the preparations.

findings.problem: Card 1 says someone is 'about to open their door to Him' and jokes about 'YOUR door' and 'your living room.' That points straight to 'home' before the baker picks. 'Boat' is also not believable for a woman in a village, so the right answer stands out. Pick wrong answers that a door and a village don't rule out, or reword card 1 so it doesn't give the answer away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Boat' is a silly fit for a woman welcoming Jesus in a village, so it doesn't sound like the other answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: No card says that Mary has chosen 'the good portion' (Luke 10:42). Card 12 asks about 'what Mary has chosen' but never says what it is. This is the key detail of Jesus's answer, so the baker leaves without it. Tell it on a story card or ask about it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Card 10 opens by repeating 'Many things,' the answer the baker just gave on card 9, before it moves on. Its joke, 'a list as long as my apron strings,' is mild and reads as pleasant, not laugh-out-loud. Cut the recap and use the card to carry the passage forward with a stronger laugh.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The apron-strings line is a nice-dad comparison, not a real laugh.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
